newsitem.title: USA: Year 2000 stocks extend gains as century-end looms.
newsitem.headline: Year 2000 stocks extend gains as century-end looms.

text.p: Shares of computer service companies specializing in the Year 2000 Bug rose sharply again on Monday as the deadline for fixing the problem looms closer.

On January 1, 2000, many of the computers that store vital information -- such as social security data, drivers' records, billing information -- are expected to crash because their software cannot handle the "00" in the date.

"This is the time of year when people remember they have to deal with the issue," said Jim Duggan, an analyst at investment bank First Albany Corp. "The companies that do this are going to be booked through the end of the century starting in the next couple of quarters."
In late morning, shares of Zitel Corp surged 10-7/8 to 72-1/8 on trading of 2.54 million shares, making it the most active stock on Nasdaq. Shares of Acceler8 Technology Corp jumped 8 to 29-1/2.
Data Dimensions Corp was up 2-1/2 at 40-1/4. Computer Horizons Corp, another computer service company, was up 1-1/8 at 36-7/8.
Duggan said the stock of almost any company that deals remotely with the Year 2000 issue will continue to rise, as anxiety about a possible worldwide computer crash grows.
Company directors and executives are starting to worry about the issue because they could be held liable for not acting quickly enough to prevent a crash, Duggan said.
According to various forecasts, companies around the world may have to spend as much as $200 billion to fix computer programs that cannot handle dates with 2000.
-- Kourosh Karimkhany, in Los Angeles, +1 800 330 NEWS
